IR.rationale: Falling short rates with a steepening curve describe monetary easing. Easing lowers funding costs for levered arbitrage strategies and supports the carry and duration positions held by macro and fixed-income funds.

B.rationale: Falling high-yield and EM corporate yields mark easy credit conditions. Event-driven, distressed and arbitrage strategies earn credit and liquidity premia in that environment, and these returns persist.

V.rationale: High implied volatility raises the liquidity and risk premia that hedge funds collect as providers of insurance and liquidity, so it carries information about subsequent returns.

AP.rationale: Hedge funds carry net beta to global equities. Reported returns are smoothed by illiquid holdings (Getmansky-Lo-Makarov), so lagged market strength feeds into subsequent index returns.

TF.rationale: Bond trend-straddle payoffs signal persistent trends in rates. Fung and Hsieh show these trends drive CTA and macro returns, and trends tend to continue.

ST.rationale: A strong momentum factor indicates a trending cross-section of stocks. Equity long/short and quantitative funds tilt toward that environment and profit from it.

FX.rationale: A weakening yen together with a strengthening Aussie dollar marks a risk-on, carry-friendly regime. Macro funds and levered funds benefit from that regime.

COM.rationale: Rising broad commodity prices signal strengthening global demand. They also feed commodity trend and macro positions.

MC.rationale: Loose financial conditions combined with above-trend activity form a benign macro state. In that state leverage and funding are readily available to hedge funds.

ENDG.rationale: Hedge-fund index returns are positively autocorrelated because of illiquid holdings and return smoothing, so recent strength tends to persist.

IR.rationale: Rising bill rates with a flattening curve describe monetary tightening. Tightening raises funding costs and can trigger losses in levered fixed-income and convertible arbitrage.

B.rationale: Rising junk yields while AAA yields stay flat or fall is a flight to quality. Widening spreads mark the deleveraging episodes in which credit, distressed and arbitrage strategies suffer tail losses.

V.rationale: High VIX combined with crisis-driven volatility news marks systemic stress. Under such stress hedge-fund returns become more correlated and short-volatility exposures produce large losses.

AP.rationale: Global equity selloffs spill into hedge funds through net beta and margin calls. Smoothing then carries the losses into following months.

TF.rationale: Large stock trend-straddle payoffs signal extreme equity moves. Most non-CTA strategies are implicitly short such lookback options, so they lose in these moves.

ST.rationale: Momentum crashes coincide with abrupt factor reversals and crowded-trade unwinds. These unwinds hurt equity long/short and quantitative strategies.

FX.rationale: A strengthening yen with a weakening Aussie dollar is a carry unwind. Carry unwinds coincide with funding-liquidity stress and forced hedge-fund deleveraging.

COM.rationale: Falling oil and copper prices signal a global demand shock. Such shocks hurt EM, energy-heavy event-driven and distressed books.

MC.rationale: High financial stress combined with weak real activity is a recessionary-stress state. Drawdowns in that state are deep and persistent.

ENDG.rationale: Poor recent returns tend to be followed by further losses. Smoothing, redemptions and forced deleveraging all propagate drawdowns.

IR.rationale: Aggressive easing with bull steepening accompanies policy responses to stress. Strong rebounds in arbitrage and credit strategies follow these responses.

B.rationale: Sharply falling risky-bond yields signal credit relief rallies. Distressed, event-driven and arbitrage funds post outsized gains in these rallies.

V.rationale: Elevated volatility widens the return distribution. It also precedes rebounds as liquidity premia are harvested, so it raises the chance of upper-tail outcomes.

AP.rationale: Strong global equity rallies, transmitted through beta and smoothing, raise the probability of very strong hedge-fund returns.

TF.rationale: Strong trends at once in commodities and bonds are the environment in which CTAs and macro funds earn their largest gains.

ST.rationale: A persistently strong momentum factor rewards the trend-following tilts common in equity hedge and quantitative funds.

FX.rationale: Large currency trend-straddle payoffs mark strong FX trends. Trend-following and macro strategies capture these trends.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity rallies signal reflation. Reflation supports commodity-trend, EM and energy-exposed event strategies.

MC.rationale: Elevated financial stress increases mispricing and dispersion. Recovery from such stress produces the largest hedge-fund gains.

ENDG.rationale: Positive return autocorrelation from smoothing and trend persistence makes strong recent returns predictive of further strong returns.
